messages:
jenna: heads-up, a customer reported SSO onboarding failing during SCIM push. 403 on provisioning for a handful of users.
marc: which idp? okta or azure?
jenna: Okta (org: acme-inc). Logs show `scim-provisioner: 403 Forbidden` + `kms: decryption failed` in same trace.
rachel: that smells like KMS envelope mismatch — did we rotate keys last night?
vikram: we did a dry-roll of the KMS alias at 03:05 UTC for a subset of tenants. nothing global, but acme is on the canary group.
jenna: can someone confirm whether the old alias was still being accepted by the private deployment agent? acme is on Private.
sam: pulled logs from the customer gateway: `decrypt: failed to unwrap key: invalid_envelope_header` then SCIM request aborted.
idp-bot: NOTE: SAML assertions from acme are valid; audience check passes. This is failing during SCIM post-authz.
marc: OK — two parallel issues: 1) KMS unwrap error causing SCIM to abort, 2) RBAC change in last deploy could have dropped provisioning perms. Anyone saw the RBAC PR?
emily: PR #1427 adjusted `provisioner:write` role membership last week. @marc I linked the change to the dedicated-provisioners group.
vikram: checking deploy graph... yes that PR rolled at 02:50 UTC to dedicated and private pools. It should not remove existing service accounts but might have changed role mapping.
rachel: can we quickly validate audit logs for the `scim-service` principal? if KMS decryption failing we should still see audit entries for the key usage.
security-alerts: Alert: S3 audit-logs ingestion lagged 12m around 03:10 UTC; some KMS usage events might be delayed in the console.
jenna: customer-facing: sending a quick note — "We're investigating an SSO provisioning error, potential KMS / role mapping issue; minimal user impact" :ear:
marc: low-risk triage steps: 1) snapshot current KMS alias mapping for acme, 2) verify `kms:Decrypt` audit events for scim-service, 3) check RBAC diff for provisioner principal.
sam: ran `gcloud kms keys versions list --location=us-central1 --keyring=redwood-secrets --key=provisioner` — current primary version is v3, previous v2 still has policy binding but alias points to v3.
vikram: if envelope header changed between v2->v3 (we switched to AES_GCM_RAW for v3), some clients expecting a different wrapping algorithm will fail.
rachel: that matches `invalid_envelope_header`. Private agent was built before AES_GCM_RAW support. need a patch to accept both types or roll back alias.
emily: workaround: re-point acme's alias back to v2 -> that'll restore decryption immediately. but we need to weigh rollback vs patch.
marc: incident play: rollback alias for acme, validate SCIM provisioning resumes, then follow with a coordinated patch to private agent to support AES_GCM_RAW and a key-rotation post-checklist.
security-alerts: Vulnerability note: CVE-2026-XXXX in older `kms-client-go` causes silent fallback to insecure wrapping if header mismatch not handled — triage required.
jenna: omg we need to ensure no silent fallback. can `security` run vuln triage and confirm exploitability in our build?
security: will triage. initial check: we depend on `kms-client-go v1.4.2` — upstream patched in v1.4.5. Scheduling update.
sam: meanwhile, acme verified that SCIM requests resume after we temporarily rebind alias->v2 at 04:00 UTC. provisioning backlog cleared.
vikram: rolling patch: private-agent v2.3.5 will include multi-algo envelope handling and pinned kms-client-go v1.4.5. target deploy 08:00 UTC.
rachel: postmortem action items: - add key-wrap-algo test in infra-e2e - audit any other private agents pinned pre-AES_GCM_RAW - document rotation checklist (pre-warm + canary + agent compatibility check)
emily: also add an alert for KMS-decrypt-errors > 5/min per tenant so we catch this earlier.
marc: agreed. I'll open the RBAC revert PR if we see any permission-related repro, but current root cause is KMS algorithm mismatch + missing agent support.
jenna: thanks all. I'll keep acme updated and draft an incident summary once the patch is deployed. :thumbsup:
ops-bot: deploy rollback executed: alias acme-provisioner -> v2 at 04:02 UTC by vikram (reason: emergency decryption failures).
jenna: leaving this thread open for postmortem notes. last check: provisioning green at 04:15 UTC.
marc: tagging follow-ups: @security for vuln patch, @eng-infra for e2e, @eng-ops for rollout checklist.
security: posted tracker: SEC-2026-018. will post ETA for patch by EOD.
jenna: thanks — closing loop once postmortem lands.
